items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-07-01
items.q: And then, because I played it, and Johnny Sincere, he worded it, and Piron he wrote it.

ctx.x: Uh huh. But when did he write that down? About what time?

Oh, that was, oh let me see. I was about, let's see, that piece must be about 50, let's see. Oh, I was about, let's see. I was about, I was about 20, I was in some way in my, that's over 40 years ago, 40 years ago, that's over 40 years ago, around 50 years ago, not up in there. I was calling him a boy. I was sitting down one day, in Red Light District, just sitting down playing that melody. I was sitting down playing that melody, not knowing what I was playing. See? And he walked in and he says, gee what's that…
You got a killer? You got a killer? Your big E slept off the bridge
But where did he play Herbert Lindsay? Did he play along?

No, he played all the bands. All the bands. Every band was downtown. Played in Piron's band. Sometimes Piron didn't have the band. Or sometimes they just changed one man in the band sometimes. Just one man. He said, we come to work like tonight. He said, you're the boss. All of us show up down there, the whole band show up tonight. And the whole band turned around and go back home. They go to Union Harden and New Band right there. But I can't do that today on account of Union. But all of us turned around and go…
Yeah, I never heard talk of Buddy Ford though. I don't know who that is.
